title: Vocabulary
content:
## Geometry & estimation · quick definitions
- **Adjoint:** changes a twist's reference frame.
- **Hat / vee:** rotation vector ↔ skew matrix.
- **SO(3) / SE(3):** rotation / rigid pose.
- **Exp / Log:** tangent coordinates ↔ group element.
- **Jacobian:** residual sensitivity to a local update.
- **Residual:** measurement–prediction discrepancy.
- **Covariance:** uncertainty and correlations.
- **Information:** inverse covariance.
- **Mahalanobis distance:** uncertainty-scaled residual size.
- **Gauge:** arbitrary global reference frame.
- **Observability:** which states measurements can distinguish.
- **Bias:** persistent systematic measurement offset.

## Learning · quick definitions
- **ViT:** Vision Transformer; image patches become tokens.
- **GNN:** Graph Neural Network; messages connect nodes/edges.
- **Transformer:** token processing through attention and MLPs.
- **Attention:** query–key weights combine values.
- **CNN:** shared spatial convolution filters.
- **Descriptor:** feature vector used for matching.
- **Embedding:** vector representation of an input.
- **Token:** one represented input unit.
- **Pooling:** summarize many features into fewer features.
- **Ablation:** remove a component; test its contribution.
- **Inductive bias:** assumptions favored by model structure.
- **Overfitting:** training fit that generalizes poorly.

## Robotics & optimization · quick definitions
- **Odometry:** incremental relative-motion estimation.
- **SLAM:** jointly estimate pose and map.
- **Loop closure:** constraint from a recognized revisit.
- **ICP:** alternate correspondence and local alignment.
- **Kabsch:** fixed-match rigid least-squares SVD fit.
- **RANSAC:** random minimal fits; find consensus.
- **Gauss–Newton:** linearize residuals; solve least squares.
- **LM:** adaptively damp Gauss–Newton steps.
- **Huber loss:** quadratic center; linear tails.
- **ATE / RPE:** trajectory / relative-motion error.
- **SIL / HIL:** simulated system / real-hardware test loop.
- **TF:** time-indexed coordinate-frame transforms.
